content.text:
I traced the history of the modified files and found that all the core logic defects fixed by the bug-fix commit trace back to a single commit that originally introduced `OrderedScheduler.java`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: ce628a5d74a9984998675acfd043d7ba4f1e6783

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit (2c001a55) touches `OrderedScheduler.java`, `ServerConfiguration.java`, and `BookieRequestProcessor.java`, plus adds new tests (`OpStatTest`, `TestStatsProvider`) that validate stats correctness. The most semantically meaningful (non-additive) change is in `OrderedScheduler.java`, where actual buggy logic is corrected rather than new functionality merely being added. I used `git blame` on the pre-fix version of `OrderedScheduler.java` and `git log --follow -p` to trace each changed line back to its origin, which pointed to commit `ce628a5d7` — the commit that originally introduced `OrderedScheduler.java` as a new file on 2017-10-03.

**(2) Specific defect introduced:** In `ce628a5d7`, the newly-added `TimedRunnable.safeRun()` method contained:
```java
taskPendingStats.registerSuccessfulEvent(initNanos, TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);
```
This records the raw `initNanos` timestamp (an absolute nanoTime value) as if it were a latency/duration, instead of computing the actual elapsed time since the task was queued (`MathUtils.elapsedNanos(initNanos)`). This produces wildly incorrect (huge) "task_queued" stats. The fix commit corrects this to:
```java
taskPendingStats.registerSuccessfulEvent(MathUtils.elapsedNanos(initNanos), TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);
```
Additionally, the same original commit defined `submitOrdered(long orderingKey, ...)` and `submitOrdered(int orderingKey, ...)` to call `chooseThread(orderingKey).execute(r)` directly — bypassing the `timedRunnable(r)` wrapper used elsewhere (e.g., in `submit()` and the `Object`-keyed `submitOrdered`). This means tasks submitted via these two overloads never got wrapped in `TimedRunnable` at all, so their queueing/execution stats were never recorded. The fix corrects both to call `chooseThread(orderingKey).execute(timedRunnable(r))`, consistent with the other submission methods.

**(3) Evidence:** `git blame` on the OrderedScheduler.java content just before the fix commit shows lines 146–167 (the `TimedRunnable` class, including the buggy `registerSuccessfulEvent(initNanos, ...)` call) all attributed to `ce628a5d7`. Viewing the full diff of `ce628a5d7` confirms it added the entire file, including the two `submitOrdered(long/int, ...)` methods using bare `.execute(r)` instead of `.execute(timedRunnable(r))` — exactly the lines corrected in the fix commit.

I'm fairly confident about `ce628a5d7` as the origin of the `OrderedScheduler` logic bugs, since blame unambiguously attributes the buggy lines to that single commit with no intervening edits. The `BookieRequestProcessor.java`/`ServerConfiguration.java` portions of the fix commit are additive (wiring a `StatsLogger` through to the executor and adding a new `enableTaskExecutionStats` config flag) rather than fixes to pre-existing broken logic — these appear to be feature completions bundled into the same commit rather than fixes for a distinct historical regression, so I did not attribute them to a separate bug-introducing commit.
